//: Example CENTRALLY SERVED orchestrator catalog — try central config mode against this file as served by GitHub:
//use: set MCP_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG_URL=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Byggarepop/dotnet-mcp-orchestrator/main/docs/orchestrator.central.example.json in the orchestrator's env block, restart your MCP host once, and the catalog below goes live (then updates within the poll interval, default 300 s).
//rules: A central catalog must work on every consuming machine: no ${CONFIG_DIR} or ${SOLUTION_DIR} (validation rejects them). Use ${ENV_VAR} — resolved on each machine, which also keeps secrets out of this shared file — or absolute paths.
//servers: The entries below launch via npx (needs Node.js) or dotnet tool execute (needs the .NET SDK), so they work on any machine. Downstream servers start lazily on first use; the generous connectTimeoutSeconds covers the package download on a first run.

capabilities.name: tokensaver
capabilities.summary: Token-efficient source reading for .NET/web codebases: outline C#/VB files (signatures + line ranges), minify whole files of many languages, trace DI registrations.

capabilities.name: files
capabilities.//: ${USERPROFILE} resolves on each consuming machine (Windows). On macOS/Linux, change it to ${HOME}.
capabilities.summary: Read and inspect files under the user's home directory (list, read, search).

capabilities.name: Unwritten
capabilities.summary: Git-history hole detector: flags files and C# members that historically co-change with your edit but are absent, with confidence and commit evidence. Tools: check_holes, expected_companions, explain_rule, stats, reindex.
capabilities.//promote: Proactive capability: the agent must call it unprompted after edits, so its instructions are hoisted into the initialize handshake (server instructions) instead of waiting for a list_capabilities call. Keep the promoted text tight — the whole advertisement block is budgeted (see the Proactive capabilities README section).
capabilities.instructions:
Unwritten — repo convention guard. Learns which files AND code members (methods, classes) historically change together and flags expected-but-missing companion changes at both levels.

CALL THIS WHEN:
- You have made ANY code change in a git repo — modified a method, added a class, renamed something, edited config, created or deleted files — and are about to finish a task, commit, or hand back to the user → check_holes with the changed files. Works at member level too: "you changed CalculateFreight but not its tests" — so call it even when only method bodies changed.
- You are planning a change and want to know which files or members usually accompany the one you're about to touch → expected_companions.
- A hole was flagged and you need to judge whether this case is a legitimate exception → explain_rule (returns historical evidence and past exceptions).
- The user asks "did I/you forget anything?" or mentions co-change/conventions → check_holes or expected_companions.

DO NOT CALL FOR: lint/style, test execution, non-git workspaces, or code-content questions. Warnings are patterns, not rules — fix or justify holes ≥0.7.

//skills: A central catalog can also serve Agent Skills. Same machine-portability rule: directory sources with ${CONFIG_DIR}/${SOLUTION_DIR} are rejected — use git or http sources (secrets via ${ENV_VAR}, resolved on each consuming machine).
